dependency_asset_review: Reviewed the dependency-assets catalog from the successful reference run (8658 installed files inspected, 2940 candidates). `priority_matches` was empty. The only named-check candidates outside standard library/metadata noise were `arviz_base/example_data/data/centered_eight.nc` and `non_centered_eight.nc` (ArviZ "eight schools" example fixtures, unrelated to the rat-tumor endpoints and never read by the source). The scientific inputs (71 rat-tumor count pairs from BDA3 p.102) are embedded as arrays in the analysis source itself, so no distribution supplies the answer. All other candidate files are library code/tests of pymc/pymc-base/scipy/numpy/pandas/matplotlib/xarray/numba with no rat-tumor content. dependency-exclusions.json is {"files": []} with no removals declared; this passed with the final reference test.
explanation: The reference executed to completion offline on Python 3.13 with pymc 6.3.2, arviz 1.3.0, arviz-base 1.3.1, xarray 2026.9.0, pytensor 3.3.4 (g++ declared for C compilation). NUTS sampling ran the full 2 chains x 2000 tune + 2000 draws (~5 s with the compile step), all analytic-grid, plotting, and PyMC steps ran unmodified, and both declared artifacts were produced and byte-verified (analytic_marginal_posterior_grid.csv, 3,871,960 bytes; pymc_posterior_ab_X_Z.nc, 136,508 bytes). The first controlled run failed only in the appended export code: `trace.posterior[["ab","X","Z"]]` raised `NotImplementedError: Selecting via tags is deprecated...` on xarray 2026.9.0 DataTree (an upstream API removal, not an analysis failure; verified reproducible across xarray 2025.3.1–2026.9.0 and unavoidable since az.plot_rank_dist requires arviz>=1). The controller applied the one-time unused-validation export repair and the retest passed with exit code 0. Dependencing suspicions aside, scientific fidelity was checked only as far as execution: the unmodified analysis source and staged file set were byte-identical, and no data reduction or parameter change was made.
unresolved_assumptions: Posterior sample values are stochastic; artifact hashes for the NetCDF file will vary between runs (chain/draw content), while the deterministic analytic grid CSV should be stable.

The controller-repaired export (sha256 d17957761a1c464bb476a1645fca7a1f8a704fc9fd178c10e9d1b672e6aa358a) is owned by the preparation worker; the runtime repair verified both endpoints are now written but not its semantic equivalence beyond the receipt.
Reference completed in ~15 s wall time, well within the 600 s limit; memory peaked ~360 MiB of the 8 GiB limit.
